levels.add-on: one more managed piece shows it
levels.you build: code you write and run shows it

signals.question: which devices have been silent longer than N3's window, and since when
firebase: the app computes age from status.ts for the device it shows; the fleet table needs a scheduled function over /devices/*/status
aws: Fleet Indexing on the shadow's reported ts and connectivity, or a scheduled Lambda over the latest-status table
self: one SQL view: now() minus max(ts) per device, Grafana shows it

signals.question: did the broker lose this session without a clean DISCONNECT
firebase: there is no broker; onDisconnect writes exist for SDK clients, not for a REST device, so the device's own online flag cannot say false
aws: the will message on the MQTT session, delivered to subscribers and to a rule
self: the will message on the MQTT session, retained on a presence topic if you say so

signals.question: when did each session start and end, and why
firebase: none; the nearest is the device writing a boot record at start-up
aws: lifecycle events on $aws/events/presence/connected|disconnected/<clientId> with a disconnect reason
self: EMQX publishes client events; Mosquitto gives $SYS counts only, so per-client it is the will

signals.question: connections, messages a second, refused logins, storage and download against the quota
firebase: the console's usage graphs: connections, storage, downloads, load; no API for them on the free plan
aws: CloudWatch metrics per account: Connect.Success, Connect.AuthError, PublishIn.Success, RulesExecuted, plus DynamoDB and S3 metrics
self: $SYS/broker/# on Mosquitto, the EMQX dashboard, Postgres statistics; a scraper and Grafana to keep them

signals.question: how many units run each version, and which ones the rollout has not reached
firebase: a function groups status.fw across /devices, or the app lists it; nothing aggregates for you
aws: Fleet Indexing on the shadow's reported fw, or the Jobs execution summary per version
self: select fw, count(*) from latest group by fw

signals.question: which units restarted in the last day, after what (power, watchdog, panic, brownout), and which are looping
firebase: from the status record's up_s, rst and boots fields, which chapter 9 adds; nothing else sees a reboot
aws: the same fields through the shadow or the status table; lifecycle events show a reconnect but not the reason
self: the same fields; a reconnect is also visible as a will followed by a connect

signals.question: what did this unit print in the last hour
firebase: a command the device polls, and a path it writes the log to (the incubator's Send Log); a listener on that path would download it to every open app
aws: a Job or a command topic the device answers by uploading to S3 through a presigned URL
self: a command topic and an HTTPS endpoint that accepts the upload

signals.signal: OTA state per device and the rollout
signals.question: which version is each unit offered, downloading, running or has rejected, and how is the rollout going
firebase: a desired record per device and a state the device writes back (the incubator's /ota/state); the stages and the halt are a script
aws: IoT Jobs: an execution per thing with a status, a rollout rate that grows and an abort configuration that cancels at a failure threshold
self: a retained desired topic per device, a state topic back, and a script for the stages

signals.question: tell someone when offline units pass 5 % or reboots pass ten an hour
firebase: a scheduled function computes the count and sends a notification
aws: a CloudWatch alarm on a custom metric the Lambda publishes, or IoT Events
self: a Grafana alert rule on the SQL view
